title: Knowledge distillation
paper: Hinton, Vinyals, Dean 2015, Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
claim: A small student trained on a teacher's softened outputs generalises better than the same student trained on hard labels alone, and a temperature above 1 helps expose the teacher's 'dark knowledge'.
setup: Teacher distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english (67M params, 91.1% val accuracy; it was trained by its authors on full SST-2). Student prajjwal1/bert-tiny (4.4M). Both student arms see the same 1000 labelled sentences and the same number of steps; loss = 0.3*CE + 0.7*T^2*KL. Temperatures [1, 2, 4, 8], 5 seeds.
result: Student alone 68.97 ± 0.39% vs distilled: T=1 70.00 ± 0.84%; T=2 69.01 ± 2.38%; T=4 69.01 ± 2.66%; T=8 70.83 ± 1.35%. Best is distilled_T8 (+1.86 points over student alone; seed std up to 1.35).
verdict_reason: The best temperature beats the student alone by 1.86 points, which is 1.4x the seed spread. The temperature effect is not monotonic.
mismatches: The gains are small and mostly within seed noise; the paper reports clear gains on larger problems.
The student stays far below the teacher; bert-tiny with 1000 labelled examples is capacity/data limited.
The teacher was trained on the full SST-2 train set, which includes our 1000-sentence subset.
We did not use a separate unlabelled transfer set, so distillation sees no extra inputs.
